question: Who among the following was the Viceroy of India when Gandhiji led the Dandi March?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Irwin**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Lord Irwin was the Viceroy of India when Mahatma Gandhi led the Dandi March in 1930.
 
• Dandi March
 
 
• Gandhi began the Dandi March on March 12, 1930, from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi, Gujarat, to break the British salt law.
 
• He reached Dandi on April 5, 1930, and publicly violated the salt law
 
 
 
• Lord Irwin
 
 
• Lord Irwin was the Viceroy of India from 1926–1931.
 
• He was not perturbed by the threat of a salt protest and the government did nothing to prevent the march. 
 
 
 
• Gandhi-Irwin Pact
 
 
• The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on March 5, 1931, between Gandhi and Lord Irwin.
 
• The pact marked the end of the period of civil disobedience in India against British rule. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Wavell (1943–1947)**:

 
 
• Lord Wavell served as the Viceroy of India during a critical period of World War II and the subsequent Indian independence movement.
 
• His tenure saw the Bengal Famine of 1943 and the Quit India Movement.
 
• He also proposed the Wavell Plan in 1945, which aimed to ease tensions between Indian political factions, but it failed to gain traction.
 
 
 
• **Lord Willingdon (1931–1936):**
 
 
• **​** Lord Willingdon was the Viceroy of India during the early 1930s, a time marked by the Civil Disobedience Movement led by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• He adopted a repressive approach to suppress the movement, including the arrest of many Congress leaders.
 
• His tenure also saw the passage of the Government of India Act, 1935, which laid the foundation for more self-governance in India.
 
 
 
• **Lord Reading (1921–1926)**:
 
 
• Lord Reading, as Viceroy of India, dealt with post-World War I unrest, including the aftermath of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
 
• His tenure was marked by increasing nationalist activities, and he faced challenges like the Non-Cooperation Movement and the Moplah Rebellion.
 
• Despite the turmoil, he worked toward constitutional reforms, including the passage of the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.
